course.name: HVAC Technician Certification Preparation Program
course.subject: hvac
course.prerequisite_policy: Open-course enrollment; prerequisites and learner eligibility may be configured by the provider.

course_learning_outcomes: Explain HVAC/R principles and industry standards.
Identify HVAC system components and their functions.
Apply electrical theory to HVAC troubleshooting.
Interpret blueprints, wiring diagrams, and schematics.
Safely handle refrigerants according to EPA regulations.
Install, maintain, and troubleshoot heating and cooling systems.
Perform airflow analysis and duct system evaluations.
Diagnose electrical, mechanical, and refrigeration system failures.
Apply workplace safety, OSHA, and EPA regulations.
Successfully prepare for national HVAC certification examinations.

program_overview: 24-Week Online Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning & Refrigeration (HVAC/R) Program

The HVAC Technician Certification Preparation Program is a comprehensive 24-week online workforce development course designed to prepare students for careers in the Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration (HVAC/R) industry while preparing them for nationally recognized certifications such as:
EPA Section 608 Technician Certification (Required for handling refrigerants)
North American Technician Excellence (NATE) Ready-to-Work and HVAC Support Technician
Other nationally recognized entry-level HVAC certification examinations

Through interactive instruction, virtual laboratories, equipment simulations, troubleshooting exercises, quizzes, module tests, AI-assisted learning, and comprehensive practice examinations, students develop the technical knowledge, practical skills, and professional competencies needed to install, maintain, diagnose, and repair residential and light commercial HVAC systems.
Upon successful completion of this program, students will be able to:
Explain HVAC/R principles and industry standards.
Identify HVAC system components and their functions.
Apply electrical theory to HVAC troubleshooting.
Interpret blueprints, wiring diagrams, and schematics.
Safely handle refrigerants according to EPA regulations.
Install, maintain, and troubleshoot heating and cooling systems.
Perform airflow analysis and duct system evaluations.
Diagnose electrical, mechanical, and refrigeration system failures.
Apply workplace safety, OSHA, and EPA regulations.
Successfully prepare for national HVAC certification examinations.
